hardBlockers.description: FAIL when harness validation shows that the stage did not leave the required durable artifact or valid repository state.
FAIL when the specification contradicts the feature request, product brief, or confirmed Product Owner decisions.
FAIL when a product decision that materially changes scope or observable behavior remains unresolved while the stage claims completion.
FAIL when the specification adds material scope without an explicit requirement or Product Owner decision.

requirements.description: State the user or product need and the observable outcome the feature must produce.
State what is in scope and explicitly exclude adjacent behavior that could otherwise be inferred.
Specify inputs, outputs, actors, state changes, and externally visible failure behavior.
Record relevant constraints and every Product Owner decision made during the stage.
Provide concrete, independently testable acceptance criteria covering the required behavior.

dimensions.description: How precisely and unambiguously the specification communicates the intended product behavior.
dimensions.good: B requires concrete language with no material ambiguity for the next stage.
dimensions.excellent: A requires a concise specification whose terms, boundaries, and behavior remain clear under edge cases.

dimensions.description: How directly the specification can be converted into objective verification.
dimensions.good: B requires every important behavior to have an observable success or failure condition.
dimensions.excellent: A requires complete behavior coverage with minimal overlap and no implementation coupling.

dimensions.description: How well the stage surfaces and resolves product decisions that affect downstream work.
dimensions.good: B requires all material product decisions to be explicit and internally consistent.
dimensions.excellent: A requires decisions to be minimal, coherent, and supported by relevant context without speculative scope.
